_comment: Optional tech inputs. DC supply patterns are taken at battery voltage on a bench supply, per Rossmann Group's 'won't turn on' guide. Context flags nudge the suspects when the phone's history makes them likelier.

dc_readings.label: 0.4-0.8 A, board boots (black screen ok)
dc_readings.note: A normal boot draw means the main power path and CPU start; suspect the step-specific part instead.

dc_readings.label: Steady 20-40 mA, nothing happens
dc_readings.note: Rails are up but the CPU is not communicating (cracked underfill or solder balls).

dc_readings.label: 0.01-0.15 A, never boots
dc_readings.note: The PMIC starts but the CPU never boots: a partial short on a secondary rail, or a charging/USB chip fault.

dc_readings.label: Cycles 0 > 320 mA > 0 > 1.4 A
dc_readings.note: A repeating PMIC restart like this points to a short on the NAND power rail.

dc_readings.label: 2 A or more immediately
dc_readings.note: Current limit at once: usually a shorted capacitor on main power. Find it before any more restores.

dc_readings.label: 0 A, no draw at all
dc_readings.note: The PMIC is not responding: check main power for shorts, then the power button line and PMIC inputs.

context_flags.label: Screen, earpiece or Face ID flex replaced
